\section{Information-theoretic quantities, and how to read them}
\label{app:info}

Every quantity in this paper is an expectation of a code length, and the
following is the whole of what a reader needs.

Fix a distribution \(p\) over write-ups of a theorem and a model \(\pi\).
The \emph{surprisal} \(-\log \pi(x)\) is the number of nats it costs to
transmit the single write-up \(x\) to a receiver who knows \(\pi\);
arithmetic coding achieves it to within two bits, and the model is therefore
literally a code \citep{deletang2024compression}.
The \emph{cross-entropy} \(\CE(p,\pi) = \E_{x\sim p}[-\log \pi(x)]\) is that
cost averaged over the source, which is exactly what a held-out loss reports.
The \emph{entropy} \(H(p) = \CE(p,p)\) is the cost of the best possible code for
that source, and the \emph{Kullback--Leibler divergence}
\(\KL{p}{\pi} = \CE(p,\pi) - H(p) \ge 0\) is the surcharge for using the wrong
one \citep{cover2006elements}.
Hence \cref{eq:cehkl}, and hence the direction that matters throughout:
a measured loss is an \emph{upper} bound on the entropy of the corpus, tightening
as the model improves.

For two write-ups \(X\) and \(Y\) of the same theorem, the \emph{conditional
entropy} \(H(X\mid Y)\) is the cost of transmitting \(X\) to a receiver who
already holds \(Y\), and the \emph{mutual information}
\(I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X\mid Y) = H(Y) - H(Y\mid X)\) is the saving.
It is symmetric, which is why it is the natural candidate for ``the content the
two renderings share'':
the mathematics cannot be more present in one rendering than in the other
without ceasing to be shared.
It is also non-negative and bounded by either marginal, \(I(X;Y) \le
\min\{H(X), H(Y)\}\), which is \cref{eq:mathcap}.
The one caution worth repeating:
\(H\) and \(I\) are expectations under a distribution, estimated from held-out
data with a model.
They are not Kolmogorov complexity, which is the length of the shortest program
printing one particular string --- per-string, uncomputable, and defined only up
to a machine constant.
The two meet only in aggregate, and nothing here needs the shortest program.

\section{The fibre account: floors, exponents and the arithmetic}
\label{app:noise}

\paragraph{Why the floor is signal plus noise.}
\Cref{prop:floor} is one line, but the estimand it is about is worth stating
carefully.
\(L_c(N,D) = H(X_c\mid Z) + \KL{X_c}{\pi_{N,D}}\) for every trained model, so
\(\inf_{N,D} L_c \ge H(X_c\mid Z)\), with the infimum attained only in the limit
where the model is the source.
\(E_c\) in \cref{eq:chinchilla} is a fitted extrapolation of that limit.
The chain rule against the certifying term gives
\(H(X_c\mid Z) = I(X_c;X_{\mathrm{FL}}\mid Z) + H(X_c\mid X_{\mathrm{FL}}, Z)\)
with no further assumption.
Three cautions attach.
The fit can undershoot its own estimand, and demonstrably does:
the same runs yield a code floor of \(0.22\) or of nearly zero depending on the
functional form \citep{luo2025codescalingdatahungry}, and the same
natural-language data yields \(\num{scaling_fit/nl_ref/E}\) or \(1.82\) depending on the fitting
procedure \citep{besiroglu2024chinchilla}.
The estimand is a property of the corpus and the tokenisation jointly, so floors
are comparable across channels only after conversion by tokens per theorem.
And \(E\) absorbs any systematic gap the functional form cannot express, which
is the reason we read orderings under one form on one grid rather than values.

\paragraph{Where \(\alpha \approx 4/d\) comes from.}
The relation is a resolution argument rather than a fit, and everything below
substitutes into it, so it is worth having in one place.
A network with \(N\) parameters can resolve a \(d\)-dimensional data manifold
only down to cells of linear size \(s \asymp N^{-1/d}\);
a target with bounded curvature is approximated to \(O(s^{2})\) on a cell, and a
squared-error objective pays the square of that, \(O(s^{4}) = N^{-4/d}\), whence
\(\alpha \approx 4/d\) --- with \(d\) the \emph{intrinsic} dimension of the data,
not the ambient dimension of its representation \citep{sharma2022manifold}.
What makes that evidence rather than numerology is that the two sides are
measured by unrelated instruments:
\(d\) by an intrinsic-dimension estimator on the network's internal
representation, \(\alpha\) by a scaling fit, with the product found roughly
constant and of order \(4\) across teacher--student setups and real datasets.
\citet{bahri2024explaining} place the argument among the regimes --- it governs
the \emph{resolution-limited} case, where the bottleneck is how finely the
manifold can be carved, as against the variance-limited case, where the exponent
comes from sampling fluctuation and is insensitive to \(d\) --- and our
prediction is about the first.
That is also why \cref{eq:alphafibre} carries \(\kappa\) rather than a literal
\(4\):
the constant is the least robust part of the transfer, the affine structure is
what we test, and a channel-common \(\kappa\) is all that structure needs.
Two steps below are ours rather than borrowed --- the local product structure
that makes intrinsic dimension additive, and the identification of its second
factor with the fibre of a rendering.
The exponent relation is imported; the decomposition of \(d\) is the claim.

\paragraph{Why the fibre adds to the dimension.}
Locally, a rendering's data manifold factors as
\(M_c \cong M_{\mathrm{math}} \times M_{\mathrm{form}}(c)\):
a point is a choice of content together with a choice of how to realise it, and
the two are chosen independently by construction, since the fibre is exactly
what the content does not fix.
Intrinsic dimension is additive over a product, so
\(d_c = d_{\mathrm{math}} + d_{\mathrm{form}}(c)\), and substituting into
\(\alpha \approx 4/d\) \citep{sharma2022manifold} gives \cref{eq:alphafibre}.
Three consequences are worth stating separately.
The term channel has \(d_{\mathrm{form}} = 0\) and so furnishes the reference
point that turns the affine relation into a checkable prediction on three
channels rather than an unfalsifiable fit.
The relation is on \emph{reciprocals}, so equal increments of fibre dimension
buy diminishing increments of exponent --- the first rung of the tower should
gain more than the second.
And \(\kappa\) is a nuisance constant, estimated from the reference channel
rather than assumed to be exactly \(4\);
nothing here depends on its value, only on its being common to the three arms,
which the matched protocol enforces.

\paragraph{The same conclusion from discrete skills.}
Suppose content quanta have ranked use frequencies
\(p^{\mathrm{c}}_k \propto k^{-(1+a_{\mathrm{c}})}\) and form quanta
\(p^{\mathrm{f}}_k \propto k^{-(1+a_{\mathrm{f}})}\), and that a channel's
training distribution is a mixture of the two populations
\citep{michaud2023quantization}.
Merging two power-law populations gives a ranked spectrum whose large-rank
behaviour is set by whichever decays more slowly, so
\(a_c = \min(a_{\mathrm{c}}, a_{\mathrm{f}}(c))\) asymptotically, with a
mixture-weighted blend at finite rank.
Deleting the form population therefore cannot lower the exponent, and strictly
raises it whenever form is the flatter of the two.
This route predicts something the manifold route does not:
both spectra are measurable on the corpora \emph{without training anything} ---
lemma-citation frequencies on the formal side against \(n\)-gram frequencies on
the prose side --- so the fitted exponents acquire a corpus-only predictor that
can be checked against them.

\paragraph{Entropy and dimension are independent, which is what makes the theory
falsifiable.}
A fibre with \(m\) independent uniform binary choices per theorem has entropy
\(m\log 2\) and dimension \(m\).
A fibre with one choice among \(2^{m}\) styles, each deterministic given a
context the model can see, has the same entropy and dimension close to one once
that context is available.
Conversely, \(m\) nearly deterministic conventions give dimension \(m\) and
entropy near zero.
So \(H(\nu_c)\) and \(d_{\mathrm{form}}(c)\) are not functions of one another,
and an intervention on one at fixed other is possible in principle.
The synthetic dial test of \cref{sec:experiments:law} is that intervention:
generator temperature is a change of the first kind, generator style repertoire
of the second.
Any account summarising a channel's noise as a single scalar predicts the two
dials move \(E\) and \(\alpha\) together;
\cref{eq:alphafibre} predicts they separate.

\paragraph{The exponent comparison.}
For an \(s\)-smooth target on a \(d\)-dimensional domain, \(n\) samples fill the
domain at spacing \(h \asymp n^{-1/d}\), and an \(s\)-smooth function is
approximated to \(O(h^{s})\) at that spacing, giving squared error
\(n^{-2s/d}\) when the observations are exact.
Under observation noise no estimator does better than \(n^{-2s/(2s+d)}\)
\citep{stone1982optimalrates, tsybakov2009nonparametric}.
The ratio of exponents is \(d/(2s+d) < 1\), for every \(s\) and every \(d\):
noise costs a strictly flatter rate, not merely a higher floor.
\citet{cui2021noisycrossover} localise the transition --- the noiseless exponent
holds up to a crossover sample size set by the noise level, and a strictly
slower one holds beyond it --- which is what makes the penalty grow with the
budget rather than sit as a constant.
We restate the seam from \cref{sec:method:scaling}:
these are results about regression with additive observation noise, and we
import the decomposition, not the exponents.

\paragraph{The compute-optimal ratio, and why it is not a counterexample.}
Minimising \(E + AN^{-\alpha} + BD^{-\beta}\) subject to \(C \propto ND\) gives
\(\alpha A N^{-\alpha-1} = \beta B D^{-\beta-1} \cdot (D/N)\), hence
\(N_{\mathrm{opt}} \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)}\),
\(D_{\mathrm{opt}} \propto C^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}\), and
\[
  \frac{D_{\mathrm{opt}}}{N_{\mathrm{opt}}}
  \;\propto\; C^{(\alpha-\beta)/(\alpha+\beta)}.
\]
With the published natural-language fit (\(\alpha = \num{scaling_fit/nl_ref/alpha}\), \(\beta = \num{scaling_fit/nl_ref/beta}\))
the exponent is \(0.097\);
with the code fit (\(\alpha = 0.485\), \(\beta = 0.298\)) it is \(0.239\)
\citep{hoffmann2022chinchilla, luo2025codescalingdatahungry}.
A corpus with a steeper \emph{model} exponent therefore wants proportionally
more data as compute grows --- which is what ``code is more data-hungry at
compute-optimality'' reports, and it is a consequence of the steeper exponent
rather than evidence against it.
The quantity our claim concerns is the other one:
to come within \(\eps\) of a channel's own floor costs
\(D(\eps) = (B/\eps)^{1/\beta}\) tokens, so a flatter \(\beta\) is a tax whose
multiplier grows without bound as \(\eps \to 0\).

\section{Cross-entropy bounds the log search budget}
\label{app:search}

This result is not on the paper's spine;
we record it because the loss we measure has a second reading that costs
nothing to state.
Fix a goal \(t\) and a policy \(\pi(\cdot\mid t)\) over serialised candidates.
The \emph{search difficulty} is \(\Dsearch(t) = -\log\pi(A(t)\mid t)\) and the
\emph{reference cross-entropy} is \(\CE(t) = -\log\pi(\sigma(P^\star)\mid t)\),
the loss on the serialisation of one library proof, which training optimises and
a checkpoint reports for free.
Pass@1 is exactly \(e^{-\Dsearch(t)}\).

\begin{proposition}[Reference cross-entropy bounds the log search cost]
\label{prop:bound}
Let \(A(t)\) be the set of serialised terms the kernel accepts for \(t\), with
\(\sigma(P^\star) \in A(t)\).
Sampling independently at temperature one, the success probability is
\(p = \pi(A(t)\mid t) \ge \pi(\sigma(P^\star)\mid t) = e^{-\CE(t)}\), and draws
to a first accept are geometric with mean \(1/p\), so
\(\log\E[\#\text{samples}] = \Dsearch(t) \le \CE(t)\).
\end{proposition}

The argument is monotonicity of a measure under set inclusion;
what earns it a number is that three conditions are load-bearing.
\emph{(i)} \(\CE\) must be the loss on the value region whole --- every target
from the token after the type/value separator through the terminal
\texttt{<eos>}, none masked --- which is not the trainer's full-sequence loss,
the two differing by the entire type-region loss.
\emph{(ii)} The sampler must be the deployed one:
any nucleus cut or length cap that can prune a token of \(\sigma(P^\star)\)
voids the identification, and a temperature away from one moves \(p\) in no
universal direction.
\emph{(iii)} The accept set must be the kernel's;
a weaker oracle admits terms the kernel would reject.
Pulling \(A(t)\) back through any decoder gives the same inequality on any
channel, so the bound is not a property of this substrate.
What injectivity buys is that here a string log-probability \emph{is} a term
log-probability, so the slack \(\CE(t) - \Dsearch(t)\) is exactly the mass on
other accepted terms;
a channel realising one mathematical object as many strings adds a term to the
slack that says nothing about which proof was found.

\paragraph{The declaration-order admissibility rule.}
Measurement environments import the whole library, so a held-out goal
\texttt{Foo.bar} can be discharged by \texttt{@Foo.bar}:
sound, axiom-clean and worthless as evidence.
We admit an accept only if every constant it cites was already elaborated when
the goal's own declaration was, ranking constants by (module index in the import
topology, source start line) and permitting equality only within a single source
span.
Declaration order rather than the coarser module index is what keeps the
reference proof admissible:
on a pilot of \(4{,}710\) theorem rows, \(81.2\%\) of reference witnesses cite at
least one constant from their own module, so a module-index cut would discard
the reference proof for roughly four goals in five.
We report the coarse cut as a sensitivity, never as the primary arm.

\section{The object: constructors and reduction}
\label{app:expr}

Lean~4's kernel terms inhabit one inductive type whose constructors fall into
eleven kinds.
\emph{Bound variables} (\texttt{bvar}) are de~Bruijn indices counting binders
outward;
\emph{free variables} (\texttt{fvar}) name hypotheses in a local context;
\emph{metavariables} (\texttt{mvar}) are elaboration holes and must not appear in
a closed candidate.
\emph{Sorts} (\texttt{sort}) carry a universe level, with \(\mathsf{Prop}\) the
sort at level zero.
\emph{Constants} (\texttt{const}) name environment declarations together with an
explicit universe instantiation.
\emph{Applications} (\texttt{app}) are binary and curried.
\emph{Lambda} (\texttt{lam}) and \emph{dependent function} (\texttt{forallE})
abstractions carry a binder name, a domain, a body, and binder-information
determining implicitness.
\emph{Let} bindings (\texttt{letE}) carry a type, a value, and a body.
\emph{Literals} (\texttt{lit}) are natural-number or string constants.
\emph{Projections} (\texttt{proj}) select a field of a structure by index.

Reduction is by \(\beta\), \(\zeta\), \(\delta\), \(\eta\), \(\iota\), and
projection reduction.
Definitional equality is decided by \isDefEq, which interleaves weak-head
normalisation with structural comparison and a lazy unfolding heuristic.
The procedure is sound and incomplete:
an ``equal'' answer is a proof of definitional equality, a ``not equal'' answer
is a failure to find one within budget.
Because acceptance is what we count, incompleteness costs us candidates and
never costs us soundness.
The propositions-as-types correspondence \citep{curry1934functionality,
Howard1980} is why theorems and definitions share this one object.

\section{The soundness record at the pin}
\label{app:soundness}

\paragraph{Accept order.}
On a candidate \(c\) and goal \(t\) the certification routine runs:
(i) a syntactic subject guard rejecting metavariables, loose bound variables and
malformed projections;
(ii) closedness checks on \(t\) and on the reference;
(iii) kernel ratification of \(c\) against \(t\) by declaration addition ---
when no goal is supplied it instead infers a type and ratifies against that;
(iv) a transitive axiom-closure walk over the cited constants;
(v) \(\isDefEq(c, e)\) against the reference with metavariable assignment
disabled.
The certificate type's constructor is private to its module, so acceptance
cannot be minted anywhere else;
that property is pinned by a test asserting the construction fails to compile.
The kernel check is forced to run synchronously, because an asynchronous
elaboration frontend can otherwise defer it into a snapshot task that no one
awaits.
On a walked accept the trusted axiom base is contained in
\(\{\texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice}, \texttt{Quot.sound}\}\);
an empty recorded closure means ``closure not observed'', never ``no axioms''.

\paragraph{Red-team gate.}
Twenty-two adversarial probes over five suites run against the pinned verifier
and are green at the pin:
an axiom-guard suite; an in-Lean red team in a library-free environment;
a production-binary canary against the pinned library whose expected verdict
triple is \(\{\textsf{reject}, \textsf{reject}, \accept\}\);
an evaluation-side reroute probe;
and the kernel positive control below.
The probe expectations comprise five accepts, eleven rejects, three type
mismatches, one parse error, and two protocol outcomes.
The fixture is content-addressed and the verifier tree is recorded by digest, so
the gate result is reproducible against a named verifier revision rather than
against ``the code at the time''.

\paragraph{Positive control.}
We retain \texttt{leanprover/lean4\#14613}:
a misreading in the kernel's type checker of a sort that is \(\mathsf{Prop}\)
only up to universe normalisation, which permitted a projection out of a proof.
The probe asserts two independent things --- that the kernel rejects the leak,
and that no inductive in the certification environment is a hazard for it --- and
records its own reachability caveat:
the bug is real but not reachable from a stock environment.
We report it as a control that the gate can detect a real kernel defect, not as
a vulnerability we survived.

\paragraph{The defeq fidelity guard.}
Kernel ratification alone confirms that a candidate is \emph{some} well-typed
object.
Tying acceptance to definitional equality with the \emph{goal} type is what
closes the well-typed-but-wrong channel, in which an agent is rewarded for a
proxy that diverges from the intended objective
\citep{skalse2022rewardhacking}.
This matters most when kernel acceptance is used as a binary reward
\citep{lambert2024tulu3}.

\section{An instrument that did not work: guesswork bounds}
\label{app:guesswork}

We report a negative instrument result rather than omit it.
The natural information-theoretic strengthening of \cref{prop:bound} replaces
the geometric sampling model with optimal guessing:
\citet{arikan1996guessing}, following \citet{massey1994guessing} and extended by
\citet{sundaresan2007guessing}, bounds the expected number of guesses to
identify a value in terms of a R\'enyi entropy of order one half, which would
give a lower bound on search cost to complement our upper bound.
We implemented it and it is vacuous on this problem.
The bound becomes negative --- and hence says nothing --- whenever the entropy
estimate falls below roughly \(\log(1+\log M)\) for the support size \(M\)
implied by the context cap and vocabulary, which on our surface is around eleven
nats;
that is precisely the regime of the goals whose conditional distributions are
most concentrated, which is to say most of the library.
The estimator also carries its own convergence alarm, the gap between the
R\'enyi estimate and a Gaussian surrogate, and that gap is tens of nats where
the bound would otherwise be interesting.
We record this so that the next reader does not spend the same effort.
